bullets.title: AMD: MSFT Azure Helios deployment confirmed; GW-scale customer upside $15-20B/GW
bullets.body: Microsoft announced deployment of AMD Helios Rackscale for Azure AI inference, new EPYC Venice CPU VMs, and Pensando DPU networking shipping H2 2026. Wolfe sees OpenAI and Meta as GW-scale Helios customers in CY27, with each GW of MI-400 capacity driving $15-20B revenue and $3-4 EPS; AMD trades at premarket +4.9%. Wolfe frames AMD path to $25+ earnings power; Advancing AI Day on 7/23 expected to provide additional deal color.

bullets.title: MU/SNDK: MS bullish post DC checks; memory prices +25% Q2→Q3, shortages intensifying
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Joe Moore, after speaking with purchasing managers, says data center memory shortages show no signs of abating with prices up at least 25% on a like-for-like basis from 2Q to 3Q. Kimi K3 is not memory-light—MS notes it requires substantial HBM, GPUs, and scale-up networking. UBS echoes the view, calling K3 a 'DeepSeek R1 moment' with NVDA and MU as key beneficiaries; Nvidia CMX NAND demand projected to surge from 35M TB this year to 100M+ TB next year.

bullets.title: IREN: Signs $2.8B new AI contracts, raises 2026 ARR target to $4B+
bullets.body: IREN signed $2.8B in new multi-year customer contracts with leading AI developers and formally raised its full-year AI Cloud annualized run-rate revenue target to over $4B from $3.7B, with ~85% of target now under contract. Stock was up ~7.8% premarket. xAI (Colossus scaling) is speculated as the mystery customer given IREN's renewable power flexibility advantages.

bullets.title: HUT: Beacon Point 1GW campus fully commercialized with $9.8B 15-year lease
bullets.body: HUT fully commercialized its 1GW Beacon Point AI data center campus via a second 352MW lease worth $9.8B over 15 years (rising to $50.2B with renewals), with total contracted AI DC capacity reaching 949MW and $26.6B in base-term contract value. HUT redesigned its first data hall around NVIDIA's architecture, increasing capacity 57% with the same footprint. Stock was +13.5% premarket.

bullets.title: TSLA: Technical deterioration; 22V flags support break risk to $250 ahead of earnings
bullets.body: 22V Research cut TSLA's Technical Score to 1 (Weak) from 2 (Neutral), noting the stock sits beneath weakening 50- and 200-day moving averages with relative performance near 12-month lows vs. S&P 500. Key support at $350; a break implies risk to $250. Analyst recommends tactical put buys (weekly 355 puts ~$5) given implied earnings move of 5% is 'fair.' OPCO expects mixed results and extended timelines on Terafab production.

bullets.title: TXN: Strong beat setup into Q2; data center +90% YoY, options imply ~9.8% move
bullets.body: UBS expects TXN Q2 revenue/EPS of ~$5.35B/$2.01 vs. guidance midpoint, potentially above the high end, with data center growing ~90% YoY in CQ1 and autos accelerating +9.9% YoY. Consensus expects $5.25B revenue and $1.94 EPS with a ~9.8% implied move; TXN has beaten revenue consensus 15 of 20 quarters and EPS 18 of 20. FQ3 guidance could land ~$5.9B vs. Street ~$5.5-5.6B—a meaningful upside surprise.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Q2 preview (7/22); $117B revenue consensus, 6% implied move; 'Frozen v2' chip catalyst
bullets.body: StreetAccount consensus expects GOOGL Q2 gross revenue of $117.01B, EPS $2.87, with Google Cloud at $22.24B and Search at $63.42B; options imply ~6% post-earnings move. Google is separately developing 'Frozen v2,' a chip integrated with Gemini AI that could enable 6-10x efficiency gains. GOOGL +2.0% YTD vs. XLK +11.3%, has beaten EPS consensus 16 of 20 quarters.

bullets.title: INTC: UBS raises PT to $121 on DCAI strength; beat-and-raise quarter expected
bullets.body: UBS raised INTC's JunQ revenue estimate to $15.3B (from $14.8B) and SepQ to $16.4B (from $15.3B) on strong DCAI with higher CPU pricing and units. Price target lifted from $83 to $121 on higher Intel Product EBIT and peer multiples; gross margin expected in the low 40%s vs. 39% guidance despite Panther Lake headwinds. Panther Lake on 18A ramp seen driving notebook growth in CCG.

bullets.title: NOW: CLSA initiates underperform; DA Davidson and DEN expert checks remain constructive
bullets.body: CLSA initiated ServiceNow at underperform (stock -1.9% premarket), while DA Davidson flags positive partner checks showing execution momentum on acquisitions, Moveworks adoption, and agent orchestration positioning. UBS sees stable demand with a modest beat expected; cRPO forecast raised to 20% from 19.7%, with ~100bps beat on lower end of historical norm. Setup described as straightforward heading into earnings.

bullets.title: NFLX: Hedgeye bearish post-Q2; UCAN growth halved, margin inflection turned negative
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags NFLX UCAN revenue growth halved to +10% from +14% prior quarter, the worst growth in years, with Q2 operating margin at 33.4%—down 70bps YoY on a clean comp. Revenue grew +13.4% but operating income grew only +11.1%, implying negative operating leverage. NFLX also pulled its 'What We Watched' engagement report to an annual cadence, reducing disclosure on a contested metric.

bullets.title: CLS: Citi Buy; 50%+ Y/Y Jun-Q growth expected, AMD Helios ramp key; stock -17% last week
bullets.body: Citi expects CLS to report >50% Y/Y Jun-Q sales growth (above guidance midpoint of 43-54%) on hyperscale and enterprise demand, with FY26 revenue $19.1B and EPS $10.14. Investor FY27 sales expectations at $30B+ vs. Street $27B. AMD Helios ramp and 1.6T product timing are the key call topics; Dell'Oro data shows CLS lost share to Accton in Q1, a competitive concern. Stock fell 17.3% last week.

bullets.title: APP: Citi Buy; Week 29 eCommerce clients +1.3% to 10.6K; HK losses moderating
bullets.body: AppLovin's eCommerce client count reached 10,609 as of July 17 (+1.3% w/w); US store count hit 4,996, representing 64.2% of Shopify customers using AppLovin Ads. HK store share fell to 14.7%—down 640bps since last month but only 30bps w/w, suggesting dropshipper churn rather than fundamental loss. Weekly growth decelerated from 3.1% in 1Q26 to 2.2% expected in 2Q26.

bullets.title: SPOT: Rivals match price hikes; AI Music upsell scenario adds €285M-€1.1B revenue optionality
bullets.body: Apple Music raised prices following Amazon and YouTube, joining at $1 below Spotify's current level (reflecting audiobook premium)—resolving investor concerns about margin pressure from SPOT's January 2026 hike. Goldman Sachs frames AI Music as a key upside scenario: 4% penetration at €4.00 adds €285M revenue/€100M gross profit; 8% at €7.00 adds €1.1B revenue/€400M gross profit. GS calls SPOT a 'topical name' with potential to become a compounder.

bullets.title: DIS: Benchmark cuts film outlook; Moana posts $248M theatrical loss, Buy maintained
bullets.body: Benchmark forecasts Moana's global box office at $284.7M with a $248.2M theatrical loss after first 10-day box office hit only $178.5M through July 19—well below expectations. The firm attributes the miss to a misjudged remake strategy (original still widely available; sequel released just 19 months after Moana 2). Benchmark also flags Avengers: Doomsday (Dec 18) as a strategic mistake given IMAX window conflict with Dune: Part Three; maintains Buy citing DIS's diversified business.

bullets.title: DKNG: Wells Fargo cuts 2Q26 EBITDA on weak hold outcomes and higher promos
bullets.body: Wells Fargo reduced DKNG 2Q26 EBITDA estimates citing higher promotional spend in prediction market states and weaker hold outcomes during NBA Finals and World Cup. FanDuel is taking share from DraftKings. Citi separately notes prediction market volume hit 27% of US legal sports-betting during the World Cup (up from 9% at year-start), with Kalshi doubling trading records and outpacing DKNG/FLUT in mobile DAUs during the tournament.

bullets.title: GEV: OPCO likely beat-and-raise; top pick for 800V data center power transition
bullets.body: OPCO expects GEV to beat and raise on strong bookings as the primary power solutions partner for the 800V data center architecture transition, highlighting bundled solutions, margin expansion, and AI-driven manufacturing efficiencies. GEV and AMSC are OPCO's top picks for power management equipment. Morgan Stanley's Stephen Byrd is also buying the dip in onsite power plays with GEV among preferred equipment manufacturers alongside BE.

bullets.title: TSM: CFO confirms additional $100B US Arizona capex; reaffirms profitable growth confidence
bullets.body: TSMC CFO Wendell Huang confirmed an additional $100B investment in US Arizona operations driven by soaring structural AI chip demand. CFO also stated confidence in delivering profitable growth 'as long as the megatrend is right.' Goldman Sachs notes the TSM capex raise is backstopped by 'true' end-demand with no inventory buildup.

bullets.title: RBLX: Citi Buy; Week 29 CCUs -10% YoY track to low end of 2Q26 bookings guidance
bullets.body: Roblox Week 29 average peak CCUs were 16.8M, down 10% year-over-year and down 3% sequentially, tracking to 2Q26 bookings of ~$1.57B—slightly below the guidance midpoint of $1.55-1.61B and Visible Alpha consensus of $1.59B. Early 3Q26 CCU trends are consistent with a $1.89B bookings forecast. Citi maintains Buy.

bullets.title: ORCL: Project Jupiter power costs surge ~$8B above plan on fuel cell switch
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reports Oracle's Project Jupiter power system costs increased to ~$8B—likely several billion above the original plan—due to a switch to fuel cells. Separately, StreetAccount notes Oracle is struggling with cost overruns and delays at AI data center developments with CDS reaching new all-time highs. Apple's Baltra ASIC (with Broadcom) remains on track for C1H27 with no delays.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler AI capex: JPM constructive ($730B 2026, $900B+ 2027); Jefferies warns of capital destruction
bullets.body: JPMorgan maintains S&P 500 YE PT of $7,800 and remains constructive on hyperscaler capex (~$730B in 2026, $900B+ in 2027), estimating $1.7T debt capacity headroom before index concentration limits. In contrast, Jefferies strategist Chris Wood warns of massive capital destruction risk as top-5 US hyperscalers have accumulated $662B in off-balance-sheet data center lease commitments, LLMs commoditize, and token prices collapse—with value in the arms race captured by picks-and-shovels, not the hyperscalers themselves.
